hypothesis: Existing trend_long Commodities and Financials sleeves have repeat cross-window alpha. If their day-2 follow-through add-ons are capped by the generic 35% first-add-on position cap, lifting only this sector-trend add-on sleeve to 50% should improve winner capture without changing entries, exits, ranking, or SPY-relative leader behavior.
why_not_llm_soft_ranking: LLM soft-ranking remains data-limited by sparse production-aligned outcome joins, so this run used deterministic fields available in the production and backtest paths instead.

not_repeated: not a SPY-relative leader cap above 60%
not a broad sector priority reorder
mechanism_insight_check.risk: The test was adjacent to prior sector sleeve and add-on-cap work, so it needed strict three-window proof and no production/backtest drift.

parameters.single_causal_variable: first follow-through add-on max position cap for trend_long Commodities/Financials sleeve
parameters.rollback: Temporary shared-policy code was removed after Gate 4 because the primary metrics were exact nulls.

market_regime_summary.mid_weak: rotation-heavy bull where strategy makes money but lags indexes
market_regime_summary.old_thin: mixed-to-weak older tape with lower win rate

delta_metrics.gate4_basis: Rejected: no canonical window changed at all, so the proposed cap did not release incremental realized capital.

gate4_result.basis: The experiment failed every positive Gate 4 criterion because all metrics were strict nulls.

production_impact.notes: The temporary implementation changed both production_parity and backtester paths during measurement, then was rolled back before commit.

rejection_reason: The current accepted add-on stack is not constrained by the generic 35% cap for this sector-trend sleeve in the fixed windows. Adding a new cap branch would add complexity with zero measured benefit.
next_retry_requires: Do not retry sector-trend first-add-on cap lifts without an add-on event audit proving cap_no_room or clipped requested_shares in this sleeve.
If lifecycle add-on work resumes, use a different quality discriminator such as event/news context or forward-observed add-on failure attribution.
Avoid further cap-only add-on experiments unless the affected_addon_count is non-zero before the backtest run.
notes: Alpha search, not measurement repair. LLM soft-ranking and SEC/event sleeves stayed blocked or data-limited, so this tested an unblocked deterministic lifecycle allocation hypothesis. The result shows the next useful lifecycle work should be trigger quality, not another cap lift.
